title: Best AI Voice Cloning 2026: Tested Picks & Real-World Reviews
description: Compare ElevenLabs, PlayHT, Murf, Cartesia and Descript voice cloning in 2026: real pricing, clone quality, languages and commercial rights.
short_desc: ElevenLabs, PlayHT, Murf, Cartesia and Descript compared on 2026 pricing, clone quality and commercial rights.
tldr_pick: ElevenLabs Creator ($22/mo) is the top pick: reference-grade clone quality at 4.2-4.5 MOS, the cheapest self-serve route to Professional Voice Cloning, and commercial rights from the $5 Starter tier.
key_takeaways: ElevenLabs leads on published clone quality and is the only platform under $30/mo with Professional Voice Cloning.
PlayHT covers 142+ languages against ElevenLabs' 32+, which decides multi-market localisation work.
Cartesia Sonic is the cheapest at roughly $0.065 per 1,000 characters and the best fit for live voice agents.
Commercial rights are a plan feature - publishing a clone made on a free tier is the most common licensing mistake here.
who_for: Podcasters, narrators, localisation teams and developers who need a specific voice reproduced at production quality, and who need to know which plan tier actually grants commercial rights before they publish.
methodology: We aggregated 2026 pricing and quality reporting from ElevenLabs' own pricing page, AI Prompts Hub's June 2026 cloning benchmark round-up, Datavook's 2026 voice generator review and Tajo's eight-tool use-case comparison, then cross-referenced every plan tier, character quota, commercial-rights clause and API rate against each vendor's live pricing page. Where reviewers disagreed on output quality we note both the consensus and the outlier. This is an editorial roundup built on published specifications and third-party listening tests, not a hands-on studio benchmark - every platform here has a free tier or trial so you can verify fit on your own voice before paying. Pricing verified August 2026.

faq.q: What is the best AI voice cloning tool in 2026?
faq.a: ElevenLabs, on published quality benchmarks and on price-to-capability. Its instant clones score in the 4.2-4.5 MOS range and Professional Voice Cloning unlocks at $22/month on the Creator tier, which is the cheapest route to a fine-tuned clone from any self-serve platform.

faq.q: How much audio do I need to clone a voice?
faq.a: Instant cloning needs 15 seconds to about three minutes depending on the platform, with ElevenLabs recommending around one minute of clean audio. Professional cloning needs 30 minutes minimum and three or more hours for best results.

faq.q: Can I use a cloned voice commercially?
faq.a: Only on a plan that grants commercial rights. ElevenLabs includes them from the $5 Starter tier, PlayHT and Murf from their Creator tiers, and Speechify varies by plan. Free tiers generally do not include commercial use, so publishing from one is a licensing risk.

faq.q: Which AI voice cloning tool is cheapest for high volume?
faq.a: Cartesia Sonic at roughly $0.065 per 1,000 characters, which is about a fifth of ElevenLabs' API rate. It trades some fidelity and language coverage for the lowest unit cost and lowest latency in this comparison.

faq.q: Do I need permission to clone someone's voice?
faq.a: Yes. Every major platform requires you to attest that you own or have consent to use the voice, and professional clone requests are commonly verified. Get written consent naming the platform, the permitted use and the retention period before you upload.

products.name: ElevenLabs
products.best_for: Reference-quality clones and professional voice cloning
products.summary: ElevenLabs is still the platform every other cloning tool gets measured against in 2026. Instant Voice Cloning needs about a minute of clean audio and lands in the 4.2-4.5 MOS range in published listening tests, which is the point where casual listeners stop reliably telling clone from original. Professional Voice Cloning (PVC) needs 30 minutes minimum, with three or more hours recommended, and unlocks on the Creator tier at $22/month.
pros: Highest published clone quality of any self-serve platform
Professional Voice Cloning available from $22/month rather than enterprise-only
Commercial rights unlock at the $5 Starter tier, not a mid-tier upsell
Credit system covers text-to-speech, dubbing, sound effects and music in one quota
cons: Credits are consumed across every product, so heavy dubbing eats your cloning budget
The free tier grants no commercial rights at all
44.1kHz PCM output via API is gated to the $99 Pro tier

products.name: PlayHT
products.summary: PlayHT's advantage is breadth. With 142+ languages it comfortably out-covers ElevenLabs' 32+, which matters if you localise the same script into a dozen markets. Both instant and ultra-realistic clone modes are included, and API access ships with the Creator plan rather than sitting behind a separate developer tier.
pros: Language coverage is roughly four times ElevenLabs' catalogue
API access is bundled into the standard Creator plan
Ultra-realistic mode closes most of the quality gap for narration work
cons: Entry price is over six times ElevenLabs' Starter tier
Quality on lower-resource languages is noticeably behind its English output
No meaningful free tier for evaluating a clone before you commit

products.name: Murf AI
products.summary: Murf is built around production workflow rather than raw clone fidelity. You get a timeline editor, pronunciation controls and slide-sync tooling that suit e-learning and internal-comms teams. Instant cloning is there from the Creator tier, but there is no professional fine-tuned clone option at any price.
pros: Editing timeline and pronunciation controls beat most cloning-first rivals
Genuine free tier for evaluating voice quality before paying
Predictable per-seat pricing with no credit-burn anxiety
cons: No professional voice cloning tier at all, so broadcast work is out of scope
API is locked behind the Business plan
20+ languages is the narrowest catalogue among the paid picks here

products.name: Cartesia Sonic
products.best_for: Real-time conversational agents and voice apps
products.summary: Cartesia Sonic is the pick when latency matters more than the last 0.2 MOS of fidelity. At roughly $0.065 per 1,000 characters it is the cheapest per-character option in this guide - about a fifth of ElevenLabs' API rate - and it is designed for streaming into live agents rather than rendering finished audio files.
pros: Cheapest per-character rate of any platform in this comparison
Streaming-first architecture built for live conversational latency
Pure usage billing with no monthly seat minimum
cons: English-primary; language expansion is still in progress
API-only, so there is no editor for non-technical teams

products.name: Descript Overdub
products.best_for: Podcast and video editors fixing lines after the fact
products.summary: Overdub only makes sense as part of Descript. Its value is being able to retype a misspoken line in a transcript and have your own cloned voice patch the audio in place. As a standalone cloning engine it is unremarkable; as a repair tool inside an editing timeline it saves genuine re-record sessions.
pros: Transcript-driven correction is faster than any re-record workflow
Cloning is bundled with a full video and podcast editor
Cheapest entry point of any editor-integrated option here
cons: No standalone API, so it cannot serve an application
English-primary with effectively no localisation story
Clone quality trails ElevenLabs and PlayHT on long-form narration

products.name: Speechify
products.best_for: Listening to documents, not producing published audio
products.summary: Speechify is a strong reading-assistant product and a weak production tool. The cloning feature exists, but commercial-use terms vary by plan and there is no professional clone tier or dependable production API. Skip it unless your actual job is consuming text as audio rather than shipping voiceovers.
pros: Excellent reading and accessibility experience across devices
Annual pricing works out cheap for personal listening
cons: Commercial rights vary by plan, which is a real risk for published work
No professional clone tier and only limited API access
Built for consumption, not for production pipelines
